messages:
maria: quick alert — we flipped ptq-litev2:canary last night. seeing an increase (~2%) in funcall JSON parse failures on streaming responses. example error: `funcall_parse_error: unexpected EOF while parsing object`

devon: streaming-only? or batch endpoints too?

maria: only streaming so far. mirrored production traffic to the canary and noticed control/low bytes at stream chunk boundaries that break our ndjson coalescer.

kai: can you paste the raw stream fragments from the proxy logs? if kvcache emits packed binary prefixes and the proxy treats frames as text we get escaped low-bytes.

maria: raw fragments (copied):
```
{"delta":"...\\u0000","finish_reason":null}
{"delta":"\\\"}\\n","finish_reason":"stop"}
```
When concatenated you get `...\\u0000\"}\\n` which json.loads rejects.

eval-bot: telemetry snapshot: parse_error_rate(ptq-litev2:canary)=0.023 over last 6h; baseline(raven-v2-q8)=0.0004. Top impacted routes: tool-invoke, web-search, reranker.

rachel: could the quantization step have changed token byte packing or introduced a binary compaction stage? NULs shouldn't appear in text frames.

kai: local repro with prefix-cache + continuous batching:
```
# pseudo
reqA -> stream chunk A ends with 0x00
reqB -> stream chunk B begins with '\\"}'
coalesce -> '...\\u0000\"}\\n' -> parse fails
```
Seems like the prefix kv data contains 0x00 which gets escaped by the proxy and then breaks the ndjson parser when chunks are joined.

devon: mitigation plan: (1) temporarily disable kv-prefix caching for the canary, (2) replay 1k failing traces against a stricter streaming coalescer to validate, (3) add a short-lived sanitizer that strips lone control chars before JSON parse and logs raw frames for investigation. thoughts?

maria: +1. sanitizer is a band-aid only. @kai please add sampled hex-dump instrumentation in the runtime (no PII) and a flag to avoid emitting NULs in text frames.

kai: will add hex dumps and a tiny streamer patch to ignore 0x00 when serializing text frames. also verifying transfer-encoding differences between prod and canary (chunked vs gzip).

rachel: also run FP32 vs PTQ comparison with identical batching/cache config to see if quant introduces the bytes. if FP32 is clean and PTQ produces NULs, the quant step likely mutated packing.

maria: filed INF-4289 with sample fragments and request ids. disabled kv-prefix caching at 1825551420. smoke slice shows immediate drop in parse errors. starting the 1k replay now. ETA ~40m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

devon: if sanitizer fixes >90% of failures on the replay we can promote it to production as a stopgap. otherwise rollback the canary.

maria: update 1825551834: replay done. sanitizer reduced parse failures by ~95% on the failing set. collected hex-dumps attached to INF-4289 for deeper analysis. we'll follow up after kernel/runtime inspection. :thumbsup:
